chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked him, peace be upon him, about a man who prayed and did not know whether he was in the third rak'ah or in the fourth. He said: "Then he is to act upon what his conjecture inclined toward. If he thinks that he is in the third, while in his heart there is something regarding the fourth, he should give salam quietly to himself, then pray two rak'ahs in which he recites Fatihat al-Kitab."

key_terms.الثَّالِثَةِ: the third rak'ah under consideration in the doubt
key_terms.الرَّابِعَةِ: the fourth rak'ah under consideration in the doubt
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rak'ahs to be prayed afterward
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: he gave the salam to conclude the prayer
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: Surat al-Fatihah, recited in those two rak'ahs

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts whether he is in the third or fourth rak'ah of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who becomes uncertain during salat (prayer) as to whether he is in the third or fourth rak'ah. It instructs him to act on the side toward which his supposition inclines, then to complete the prayer and perform two additional rak'ahs with Fatihat al-Kitab.
